faq: What is an AI model inventory?
A current list of the AI models your business uses, in your products, your systems and your suppliers' services, with where each runs, who owns it and whether it is approved.
Is this the same as AI security posture management, shadow AI discovery or a CASB?
Those tools watch and control how AI is used. This answers a different question: which models are in use, and can you prove it. It can sit alongside them.
Why not just ask teams and suppliers?

You should, and we help you structure the questions. Answers from people are incomplete and go out of date quickly, and a questionnaire is not evidence. The inventory gives you something to check them against.
Does it find shadow AI?
It looks for AI use that is not on your approved list, across the areas we agree in scope, and says what it could not see.
Does it cover AI inside our suppliers' products?
Where it shows up in your own estate and with the supplier's help. Where it cannot be confirmed, the report marks it open and suggests the question to put to the supplier.
Do you need agents on our endpoints or changes to our network?
We agree what access is needed before we start. We aim to work from what you already have, with read-only access, and we do not sit in the path of your live traffic.
Does it read our prompts or customer data?
No. It does not need to.
Can it show open models running on our own GPUs?
Yes, if you want that in scope.
Does it help with ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act or customer questionnaires?
It gives you the factual inventory those frameworks and questionnaires ask for. It does not certify compliance and it is not legal advice.
Which models can it flag, for example DeepSeek?
Whichever your policy rules out. Governments and customers have started naming particular models, and we flag whatever you list.
Is the report a certificate?
No. It is an attestation report that states its scope and date and says what we found in that scope. It does not claim to prove that nothing ruled out exists anywhere in your company.
How do we know the answer is complete?
The report says what was covered, what was not and our confidence in each finding. Where it is partial, we tell you, and we tell you what would close the gap.
Do UK firms have to keep an AI model inventory?

Not by a single UK rule that we can point to. Customers, suppliers and risk teams are asking the question, and frameworks such as ISO 42001 expect a register of AI in use. We will tell you if you do not need it.
How long does it take, and what does it cost?
We scope it with you first, agree a first milestone, then quote.

status_note: The checks are built and appear today inside our feasibility reports. The standalone screen is in early access.
benefits: Avoid a wasted survey
See the issue that could sink an application before you commission fieldwork.
Plan the studies
Get the list of field studies the site will probably need.
One view of the site
Land, heritage and protected-site constraints together, with how much of the site each one covers.
gets: How much of the site falls in each agricultural land grade, and how much of that rests on a detailed survey.
How much deep peat there is and how far away it is.
Listed buildings, monuments, parks and gardens, battlefields and World Heritage Sites on and around the site.
National Parks, designated landscapes and habitats, ancient woodland and wild land, with share and distance.
Flood zones, green belt, open access land, and distance to aerodromes and built-up areas.
The field studies the application will probably need.
who: Solar, battery and wind developers
Check a parcel before you pay for surveys.
Planning consultants
Start a site review with the constraints already mapped.
Land agents
Back a conversation with a landowner with evidence.
steps: A boundary, or a point and a size, and the technology.
Farmland, peat, heritage, protected sites and other constraints.
You receive the screen and the likely study list.
know: The screen covers Great Britain.
Farmland grades come mostly from predictive and provisional maps. A soil survey confirms them on the ground.
Peat depth needs probing on site. The screen reports mapped peat only.
Glint and glare, conservation areas and archaeology records are not included.
The screen does not predict a planning decision.
faq: Does it tell me if my site is best and most versatile land?
It reports how much of the site is mapped as grades 1, 2 and 3a, and how much of that comes from a detailed survey. Where the map is predictive, it says so, and a soil survey is still needed.
Does it cover Scotland?
Yes. In Scotland it uses prime agricultural land, mapped peat classes, heritage data and designations.
Which listed buildings does it count?
Those on the site and in the area around it, with the highest grades counted separately, and the distance to the nearest of each.
Does it replace a consultant's survey?
No. It helps you decide whether surveys are worth paying for.
Does it predict planning outcomes?
No. It reports constraints and the studies you will probably need. The planning authority decides.
audience_type: Solar, battery and wind developers, planning consultants and land agents
audience: For solar, battery and wind developers
card_summary: Spot the planning constraints that could stop a site, before you pay for surveys.
cta_h: Want a site screened for planning risk?

title: How do I check a UK company before I do business with it? | Arithim
description: Planned: a check on one UK company that confirms it exists and is active, shows who controls it and gives a dated source for every fact.
h1: Know who is behind a UK company before you deal with it.
sub: A planned check for know your business (KYB) work. Send a company number or name and get a summary of the company, who controls it as far as the UK register shows, and anything that deserves a closer look, with a dated source for every fact.
status_note: Not yet available. Register your interest and we will tell you when early access opens. Early access will cover UK registered companies only.
benefits: A quick first look
Confirm a company exists and is active in moments, before you spend time on it.
Flags with reasons
Anything that needs a closer look comes with a plain reason, so your team can decide.
Evidence for every item
Each fact shows where it came from and when we retrieved it.
gets: Whether the company is active, when it was incorporated, its registered office and its filing history.
The chain of companies that control it, as far as the UK register shows.
The check says clear or review. It does not tell you to accept or reject a customer.
The source and retrieval date for each item.
For energy counterparties, the renewable and storage projects the company's group holds or has applied for.
who: Accountants, lenders and platforms
Onboard UK business customers and suppliers with a sourced first check.
Energy developers
Check a landowner company or an offtaker before you sign an option or a power purchase agreement.
steps: A company number or a name.
A summary with sources, for your own team to act on.
know: UK registered companies only. Ownership chains that leave the UK stop where the UK register stops.
Ownership comes from information that companies file about themselves. We report what the register says and do not verify it.
No credit scores, politically exposed persons screening or adverse media.
It is a screening aid. It does not decide whether you meet your own legal duties.
faq: What is a KYB check?

KYB means know your business: checking that a company is real, who stands behind it and whether anything should make you look closer before you deal with it. This service supports that check. It does not make you compliant on its own.
Is the UK company check available now?
No. It is planned. Early access will start with a small group of named users.
Does it work for companies outside the UK?
No. Early access covers companies registered in the UK only.
Does it tell us whether to accept a customer?
No. It returns flags, reasons and evidence for your own team to decide.
Can I see where each fact came from?
Yes. Every item will show its source and the date we retrieved it.
Will it show me who owns the company?
It will show the chain of corporate owners recorded with Companies House. Individual owners are not shown in the current design.
audience_type: Accountants, lenders, platforms and energy developers that check UK companies
card_summary: Check who is behind a UK company, with a dated source for every fact.
cta_h: Want to hear when early access opens?
cta_p: Tell us what you check, how often and what you need to see in the result. It shapes what we build first.

faq: Does it design the system for me?
No. It tells you whether solar is likely to work and what could get in the way. It does not lay out panels or produce drawings.
Does it replace a site survey?
No. It helps you decide whether a survey is worth booking.
Can it tell me if I will get planning permission?
No. It flags known constraints such as a conservation area or listed status. The council decides permission.
Is it available now?
No. It is planned. Early access will start with a small group of named users.

contours.title: A sample address on a solar irradiance map
contours.desc: Contour lines drift across a map. A pin drops on a sample address, the lines tighten around it, and a Good fit verdict appears. Reasons follow: the roof faces south with light shading, the building is not listed or in a conservation area, and flood risk is low. A sample yield of about 3,900 kWh a year for a 3.5 kWp system counts up. All figures are samples.
